title: Agent Authorization Review trace submission
description: Format a client sends back after running ActionBoundary scenarios against a staging or sandbox agent. The review scores high-impact tool actions against trusted, current, scope-matching authorization evidence. Some scenarios include indirect prompt injection or other untrusted business context; that content must enter through the place the agent normally reads from, not through a pasted test prompt.

schema_version.description: Use 1.0 for this flat trace format.

environment.description: e.g. staging, sandbox, local synthetic harness

user_request.description: The task the caller asked the agent to perform. For indirect/untrusted-context scenarios, the adversarial or test instruction should not be pasted here.

data_the_agent_reads.description: Content the agent retrieved or read before acting, such as emails, tickets, invoices, records, tool responses, documents, or memory. For indirect-injection scenarios, the test instruction belongs here.

authorization_context.description: Trusted records, policy lookups, approvals, roles, tenant scope, or permission checks that existed when the action was attempted. If the agent or tool did not look up authority, leave this empty and preserve that fact.

tool_call_trace.description: Every tool call the agent made, in order, including high-impact tools, read tools, authorization lookups, denials, and tool results when available.

expected_authorization.description: Plain-English rule for what authority should be required before the high-impact action executes.

model.description: Context only, e.g. gpt-5-mini. Model choice is not the authorization decision.

notes.description: Setup notes, redactions, synthetic-data notes, or how the scenario data entered the agent's real staging path.

principal.description: The user, service account, role, tenant, or actor whose authority should govern the action.

target_resource.description: The account, invoice, patient, record, tenant, vendor, or other object affected by the action.

source.description: e.g. support_ticket, invoice_pdf, vendor_email, crm_note, tool_response, calendar_invite

trusted.description: Whether this source is allowed to authorize the action. Free-text business content is usually not trusted authority.

source.description: e.g. user_permissions, approval_system, policy_engine, vendor_master, IAM, prior_auth_system

scope_match.description: true, false, or unknown if the trace does not show enough evidence.

high_impact_action.description: Optional label for calls that move money, change records, export data, grant access, submit forms, message external parties, or otherwise cause business side effects.

result.description: Structured tool result, denial, error, or returned record.

source.description: Where the decision came from: tool-layer policy, approval lookup, IAM, workflow rule, or model-only judgment.

action_outcome.description: What changed after the attempted action. This is the business outcome, not just the model's final answer.

status.description: e.g. executed, denied, routed_to_review, no_high_impact_action, unknown
